problem:
Suppose that for the angles $u$ and $v,$ we have

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡u=\frac{8}{17},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡u=\frac{15}{17},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡v=\frac{3}{5}.
$$

If $v$ lies in the first quadrant, then $\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=${{field-1}}.

feedback.problem:
Suppose that for the angles $u$ and $v,$ we have

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡u=\frac{3}{5},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡v=\frac{8}{17},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡v=-\frac{15}{17}.
$$

Given that $u$ lies in the first quadrant, find the value of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v).$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, recall the difference formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

We know the values of $\operatorname{sin}⁡u$, $\operatorname{sin}⁡v$, and $\operatorname{cos}⁡v.$ To find the missing value of $\operatorname{cos}⁡u$, we can use the Pythagorean identity:

$$
{sin}^{2}⁡u+{cos}^{2}⁡u=1\,⟹\,{cos}^{2}⁡u=1-{sin}^{2}⁡u
$$

Substituting our values into the Pythagorean identity, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}⁡u & =1-{sin}^{2}⁡u \\  & =1-{(\frac{3}{5})}^{2} \\  & =1-\frac{{3}^{2}}{{5}^{2}} \\  & =1-\frac{9}{25} \\  & =\frac{25}{25}-\frac{9}{25} \\  & =\frac{16}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡u & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{16}{25}} \\  & =\pm \frac{4}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that $u$ lies in the first quadrant, where cosine is positive. So, we disregard the negative value, and we have 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡u=\frac{4}{5}.
$$

We can now apply the difference formula, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(u-v) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v \\  & =(\frac{3}{5})(-\frac{15}{17})-(\frac{4}{5})(\frac{8}{17}) \\  & =-\frac{45}{85}-\frac{32}{85} \\  & =-\frac{77}{85}\end{aligned}
$$
